In the given diagram (not drawn to scale), railway stations A, B, C, P and Q are connected by straight tracks. Track PQ is parallel to BC. The time taken by a train travelling at 90 km/hr to reach B from A by the shortest route is:
(Figure: triangle ABC with P on AB and Q on AC, PQ ∥ BC; PQ = 20 km, BC = 50 km, PB = 18 km.)
questions.solution: (d) 20 minutes. △APQ ∼ △ABC: AP/AB = PQ/BC ⇒ AP/(AP + 18) = 20/50 ⇒ 5AP = 2AP + 36 ⇒ AP = 12 km, so AB = 30 km. Time = 30/90 h = 20 minutes.

questions.question: AB and AC are two tangents to a circle, whose radius is 6 cm. If ∠BAC = 60°, then what is the value in (cm) of √(AB² + AC²)?
questions.solution: (a) 6√6. OA bisects ∠BAC so ∠OAB = 30°, OB ⊥ AB: tan 30° = 6/AB ⇒ AB = AC = 6√3. √(AB² + AC²) = √(108 + 108) = √216 = 6√6 cm.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The value of (1 + tan²A)(1 + sinA)(1 − sinA) is equal to 1.
Reason (R): cosec²A − tan²A = 1

options.a: A is true, R is false.
options.b: A is false, R is true.
options.c: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct reason for A.
options.d: Both A and R are true, and R is incorrect reason for A.

questions.solution: (a) A is true, R is false. (1 + tan²A)(1 − sin²A) = sec²A · cos²A = 1, so A is true; the identity is cosec²A − cot²A = 1, not − tan²A, so R is false.

marking_points.point: (a) A is true, R is false

questions.topic: Largest sphere inside a cube — assertion and reason
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The surface area of largest sphere that can be inscribed in a hollow cube of side 'a' centimetre is πa² cm².
Reason (R): The surface area of a sphere of radius 'r' is (4/3)πr³

options.a: A is true, R is false.
options.b: A is false, R is true.
options.c: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct reason for A.
options.d: Both A and R are true, and R is incorrect reason for A.

questions.solution: (a) A is true, R is false. The largest sphere has r = a/2, so its surface area = 4π(a/2)² = πa². (4/3)πr³ is the volume of a sphere, not its surface area, so R is false.

marking_points.point: (a) A is true, R is false

questions.topic: Angle in semicircle, angle at centre, exterior angle
questions.question:
AB and CD intersect at the centre O of the circle as given in the diagram. If ∠EBA = 33° and ∠EAC = 82°, find (a) ∠BAE (b) ∠BOC (c) ∠ODB
(Figure: AB is a diameter; E is on the upper arc and C on the lower arc near B; CO produced and BE produced meet at D outside the circle; AE, AC are chords.)
questions.solution:
(a) ∠AEB = 90° (angle in a semicircle). In △AEB, ∠BAE = 180° − 90° − 33° = 57°.
(b) ∠BAC = ∠EAC − ∠BAE = 82° − 57° = 25°. ∠BOC = 2∠BAC = 50° (angle at centre is twice the angle at the circumference).
(c) D, E, B are collinear and D, O, C are collinear, so ∠OBD = ∠ABE = 33° and ∠BOC is the exterior angle of △ODB: ∠BOC = ∠ODB + ∠OBD ⇒ 50° = ∠ODB + 33° ⇒ ∠ODB = 17°.
questions.figure_desc: Circle with diameter AB through centre O; E on upper arc, C on lower arc; line DOC through O and line DEB meet at D outside the circle; AE and AC drawn.

questions.topic: Number of terms from a given sum
questions.question: The sum of a certain number of terms of the Arithmetic Progression (A.P.) 20, 17, 14, .... is 65. Find the: (a) number of terms. (b) last term.
questions.solution:
a = 20, d = −3, Sₙ = 65. Sₙ = n/2[2a + (n − 1)d] ⇒ 65 = n/2[40 − 3n + 3] ⇒ 130 = 43n − 3n² ⇒ 3n² − 43n + 130 = 0 ⇒ (n − 10)(3n − 13) = 0 ⇒ n = 10 (n = 13/3 rejected, not a natural number).
(a) Number of terms = 10.
(b) Last term T₁₀ = 20 + 9(−3) = −7.

questions.topic: Cylinder with hemispherical and conical holes
questions.question: A hemispherical and a conical hole is scooped out of a solid wooden cylinder. Find the volume of the remaining solid where the measurements are as follows. The height of the cylinder is 7 cm, radius of each of hemisphere, cone and cylinder is 3 cm and height of cone is 3 cm. Give your answer correct to the nearest whole number. (π = 22/7)
questions.solution:
Volume of cylinder = πr²H = 22/7 × 9 × 7 = 198 cm³.
Volume of cone = ⅓πr²h = ⅓ × 22/7 × 9 × 3 = 198/7 cm³.
Volume of hemisphere = ⅔πr³ = ⅔ × 22/7 × 27 = 396/7 cm³.
Remaining = 198 − (198 + 396)/7 = 1386/7 − 594/7 = 792/7 ≈ 113.14 ≈ 113 cm³.

questions.topic: Triangle, circle locus and angle-bisector locus
questions.question:
Use ruler and compasses only for the following question. All construction lines and arcs must be clearly shown.
(a) Construct a △ABC in which BC = 6.5 cm, ∠ABC = 60°, AB = 5 cm
(b) Construct the locus of points at a distance of 3.5 cm from A
(c) Construct the locus of points equidistant from AC and BC.
(d) Mark 2 points X and Y which are at distance of 3.5 cm from A and also equidistant from AC and BC. Measure XY.
questions.solution:
(a) Draw BC = 6.5 cm; at B construct ∠60° with compasses; cut BA = 5 cm; join AC.
(b) The locus of points 3.5 cm from A is a circle with centre A and radius 3.5 cm.
(c) The locus of points equidistant from AC and BC is the bisector of ∠ACB; construct it with compasses.
(d) The bisector of ∠C cuts the circle at two points X and Y; these are 3.5 cm from A and equidistant from AC and BC. On measuring, XY ≈ 5.2 cm (calculated value ≈ 5.16 cm: distance of A from the bisector ≈ 2.36 cm, half-chord = √(3.5² − 2.36²) ≈ 2.58 cm).

Smriti invest a sum of money in ₹50 shares, paying 15% dividend quoted at 20% premium. If its annual dividend is ₹600, calculate:
(a) the number of shares she bought.
(b) the total investment.
(c) The rate of return on her investment.
questions.solution:
F.V. = ₹50, M.V. = 50 + 20% of 50 = ₹60. Dividend per share = 15% of 50 = ₹7.50.
(a) Number of shares = 600/7.5 = 80.
(b) Total investment = 80 × 60 = ₹4,800.
(c) Rate of return = 7.5/60 × 100 = 12.5% (equivalently 600/4800 × 100).

questions.question:
Solve the following inequation, write the solution set and represent it on the number line
−x/3 ≤ x/2 − 1⅓ < 1/6, x ∈ R
questions.solution:
Left part: −x/3 ≤ x/2 − 4/3 ⇒ −2x ≤ 3x − 8 ⇒ 8 ≤ 5x ⇒ x ≥ 8/5 = 1⅗.
Right part: x/2 − 4/3 < 1/6 ⇒ 3x − 8 < 1 ⇒ x < 3.
Solution set = {x : 1⅗ ≤ x < 3, x ∈ R}. On the number line: filled dot at 1.6, hollow (open) circle at 3, thick line between them.

marking_points.point: solution set with closed dot at 1.6 and open dot at 3

questions.question: Prove that: (sin A + cosec A)² + (cos A + sec A)² = 7 + tan²A + cot²A
questions.solution:
LHS = sin²A + cosec²A + 2 sin A cosec A + cos²A + sec²A + 2 cos A sec A
= (sin²A + cos²A) + 2 + 2 + cosec²A + sec²A (since sin A cosec A = cos A sec A = 1)
= 1 + 4 + (1 + cot²A) + (1 + tan²A)
= 7 + tan²A + cot²A = RHS.

marking_points.point: use sin A·cosec A = cos A·sec A = 1
sin² + cos² = 1; cosec² = 1 + cot², sec² = 1 + tan²

questions.topic: Inradius of a right triangle using equal tangents
questions.question:
In the given figure, PQ = 24 cm, QR = 7 cm and ∠PQR = 90°. Find the radius of the inscribed circle.
(Figure: right triangle PQR with the right angle at Q and a circle inscribed touching all three sides.)
questions.solution:
PR = √(24² + 7²) = √625 = 25 cm.
Let the radius be x. With centre O touching PQ at B, QR at A and PR at C, OBQA is a square, so QB = QA = x. Then PB = PC = 24 − x and RA = RC = 7 − x (tangents from an external point are equal).
PR = PC + CR ⇒ 25 = (24 − x) + (7 − x) ⇒ 2x = 6 ⇒ x = 3 cm.

marking_points.point: equal tangents: PC = 24 − x, CR = 7 − x

questions.topic: GST bill with an exempt item
questions.question:
The following bill shows the GST rate and the marked price of items (Shree Groceries):
S No. | Item | Marked Price (₹) | Quantity | Rate of GST
1 | Wheat Flour (unpacked) | 38 | 5 kg | x %
2 | Basmati Rice (Branded & Packed) | 180 | 5 kg | 5 %
3 | Surf Excel Quick Wash Detergent | 220 | y kg | 18 %
Find: (a) the value of x if the total GST on wheat flour and basmati rice is ₹45.
(b) the value of y, if CGST paid for detergent powder is ₹39.60.
(c) total amount to be paid (including GST) for the above bill.
questions.solution:
Wheat flour cost = 38 × 5 = ₹190; rice cost = 180 × 5 = ₹900, GST on rice = 5% of 900 = ₹45.
(a) x% of 190 + 45 = 45 ⇒ x = 0 (unpacked wheat flour is exempt).
(b) CGST = 9% of 220y = 19.8y = 39.60 ⇒ y = 2 kg.
(c) Detergent cost = ₹440, GST = 18% of 440 = ₹79.20. Total cost = 190 + 900 + 440 = ₹1,530; total GST = 0 + 45 + 79.20 = ₹124.20. Amount payable = ₹1,654.20.

questions.topic: Shadow length at two sun altitudes
questions.question: The shadow of a tower standing on a level ground is found to be 40 m longer when the sun altitude is 30° than when it is 60°. Find the height of the tower correct to the nearest m.
questions.solution:
Let height AB = h and the shorter shadow BC = x. tan 60° = h/x ⇒ h = √3x. tan 30° = h/(x + 40) ⇒ x + 40 = √3h = 3x ⇒ x = 20 m.
h = 20√3 = 20 × 1.732 = 34.64 m ≈ 35 m.

questions.question:
Draw the ogive for the following distribution:
Daily income (₹): 600-700, 700-800, 800-900, 900-1000, 1000-1100, 1100-1200, 1200-1300
No. of employees: 40, 68, 86, 120, 90, 40, 26
Hence, determine:
(a) the median income.
(b) the number of employees whose daily income exceeds rupees 1180.
(c) the upper quartile.
(d) the number of employees earning less than ₹750.
questions.solution:
Cumulative frequencies: 700→40, 800→108, 900→194, 1000→314, 1100→404, 1200→444, 1300→470. Plot (600, 0), (700, 40), (800, 108), (900, 194), (1000, 314), (1100, 404), (1200, 444), (1300, 470) (e.g. 2 cm = ₹100, 2 cm = 50 employees) and join by a smooth curve.
(a) N = 470; median = (N/2)th = 235th value ≈ ₹934 (interpolation 934.2; the answer key reads ₹940 from its graph).
(b) At ₹1180 the ogive reads ≈ 436 (key: 435), so employees earning more than ₹1180 ≈ 470 − 436 ≈ 34 (key: 35).
(c) Upper quartile = (3N/4)th = 352.5th value ≈ ₹1043 (interpolation 1042.8; key reads ₹1035).
(d) At ₹750 the ogive reads ≈ 74 (key: 75) employees earning less than ₹750.

questions.question: If a, b and c are in continued proportion, then prove that: (a² − b² + c²)/(a⁻² − b⁻² + c⁻²) = b⁴
questions.solution:
Since a, b, c are in continued proportion, b² = ac.
Numerator = a² − ac + c².
Denominator = 1/a² − 1/b² + 1/c² = 1/a² − 1/(ac) + 1/c² = (c² − ac + a²)/(a²c²).
LHS = (a² − ac + c²) × a²c²/(a² − ac + c²) = a²c² = (ac)² = (b²)² = b⁴ = RHS.

questions.question: Find the value of p for which the quadratic equation (p + 1)x² − 6(p + 1)x + 3(p + 9) = 0 has equal roots.
questions.solution:
For equal roots b² − 4ac = 0: 36(p + 1)² = 12(p + 1)(p + 9) ⇒ 3(p² + 2p + 1) = p² + 10p + 9 ⇒ 2p² − 4p − 6 = 0 ⇒ p² − 2p − 3 = 0 ⇒ (p − 3)(p + 1) = 0 ⇒ p = 3 or p = −1.
p = −1 is rejected since the coefficient of x² would be 0. Hence p = 3.

questions.topic: Successive reflections in axes and origin
questions.question:
Point P(2, −3) on reflection becomes P'(2, 3).
(a) Name the line of reflection (say L1).
(b) Point P' is reflected to P" along the line (L2), which is perpendicular to the line L1 and passes through the point, which is invariant along both axes. Write the coordinates of P".
(c) Name and write the coordinates of the point of intersection of the lines L1 and L2.
(d) Point P is reflected to P"' on reflection through the point named in the answer of part (c) of this question. Write the coordinates of P"'. Comment on the location of the points P" and P"'.
questions.solution:
(a) (x, y) → (x, −y): L1 is the x-axis (y = 0).
(b) The point invariant under reflection in both axes is the origin; the line through it perpendicular to the x-axis is the y-axis, so L2 is the y-axis. P'(2, 3) → P"(−2, 3).
(c) L1 and L2 meet at the origin O(0, 0).
(d) Reflection of P(2, −3) in the origin: P"'(−2, 3). P" and P"' have the same coordinates, so they are coincident points.

questions.question: In a class test, the sum of Harmanpreet's marks in Mathematics and English is 30. Had she got 2 more marks in Mathematics and 3 marks less in English, the product of marks would have been 210. Find her marks in the 2 subjects.
questions.solution:
Let Maths = x, English = 30 − x. (x + 2)(27 − x) = 210 ⇒ 27x − x² + 54 − 2x = 210 ⇒ x² − 25x + 156 = 0 ⇒ (x − 12)(x − 13) = 0 ⇒ x = 12 or 13.
Maths 12, English 18; or Maths 13, English 17 (both satisfy the conditions).

(Graph: histogram of height (in cm) against number of students; scale x-axis 2 cm = 10 cm, y-axis 2 cm = 5 students; bars 120-130: 6, 130-140: 29, 140-150: 34, 150-160: 22, 160-170: 12; mode located by the crossing lines in the tallest bar.)
